`GET /groups/{pacticipant_name}`: a CSV adjacency description of the
connected component of the integration graph containing this
pacticipant — mirrors `PactBroker::Api::Resources::Group` /
`RelationshipsCsvDecorator`. Unlike `get_pacticipant_network` above
(direct neighbors only, JSON), this does a full BFS transitive closure
over `integrations` (a consumer three hops away through intermediate
integrations is still included), matching
`Groups::Service#ids_of_integrations_connected_to`.
get.description:
Each row is `[pacticipant_id, name, 1, 1, 0, order, ...adjacency]`,
where `order` is the 1-based position the pacticipant was first
encountered in (consumers/providers are discovered in integration
iteration order) and the trailing columns are the `order` values of
every pacticipant this row's pacticipant is a consumer for, `0`-padded
so every row has the same length — this is what
`spec/integration/endpoints/group_spec.rb` calls "a body" without
asserting its exact shape.

post.summary:
Records a deployment of a pacticipant version to an environment. This is
the route the Pact CLI's `record-deployment` command actually uses,
discovered via the version resource's `pb:record-deployment` links —
unlike the flat `POST /deployed-versions` below, which Ruby doesn't have.
post.description:
Mirrors Ruby's record_deployment_spec.rb: deploying the same version to
the same environment+instance again is idempotent (returns the existing
row, marks nothing as undeployed); deploying a *different* version marks
the previous currently-deployed version for that pacticipant+environment+
instance as undeployed, without touching other instances/environments.

404.description: Pacticipant, version, or environment not found

post.summary:
Mirrors Ruby's record_release_spec.rb: releasing an already-released
version is idempotent (same uuid, unchanged createdAt); releasing a
version that was previously released but had its support ended flips
`currentlySupported` back to true and bumps `updatedAt`, but does not
touch `createdAt`. Unlike deployment, a release does *not* end support
for any other version — multiple versions can be concurrently supported
in the same environment (e.g. mobile app rollouts).

BranchVersion.description:
Mirrors Ruby's `EmbeddedBranchVersionDecorator`.

The branch name is rendered as `name`, not `branch` — the decorator carries
its own "TODO rename this to branchName in next major version" — and
`latest` says whether this version is the head of that branch.

oneOf.description:
`null` for a provider that hasn't verified the pact, as in Ruby's
`MatrixDecorator#provider_hash`.

EnvironmentRef.description:
An environment a version is deployed to or released in, as Ruby's
`EmbeddedEnvironmentDecorator` renders it.

contacts.description:
Ruby omits `contacts` entirely when none were supplied on create, and
only renders the key once there is something to render.

updatedAt.description:
Ruby's `Timestamps` renders `updatedAt` only when it differs from
`createdAt`, so it is absent on an environment that has never been
updated.

IntegrationParticipant.description:
Ruby renders the two ends of an integration as pacticipant objects, not as
bare name strings.

oneOf.description:
`null` for a provider that hasn't verified the pact. Ruby's
`MatrixDecorator#provider_hash` seeds the hash with `version: nil` and
only fills it in once `line.provider_version_number` is non-nil.

MatrixResponse.description:
The `/matrix` response body.

Ruby's `MatrixDecorator#to_hash` returns exactly three top-level keys and no
`_links`:

```text
{ summary: { deployable, reason, success, failed, unknown, ignored? },
  notices: [ … ], matrix: [ … ] }
```

(`ignored` is only present when the request had ignore selectors, and
`summary` is `{ deployable, reason }` merged with
`DeploymentStatusSummary#counts`.) Nesting the rows under `_embedded` and
flattening the summary to the top level, as this once did, is a shape the Ruby
broker never serves — and the consumer's own matchers assert
`$.body.matrix` and `$.body.summary` are present.

branches.description:
The same list as `branchVersions`. Ruby's `MatrixDecorator` renders
both keys from the same `branches(...)` call — its own comment marks
this one "TODO delete this" — so a client written against either key
works against either broker.

PacticipantRequest.description:
A pacticipant request body (Ruby's `PacticipantSchema`). `POST
/pacticipants` reads only `name`; `PUT`/`PATCH` validate the raw JSON with
`parse_pacticipant_body` so that an explicit `null` can be told apart from
an absent key, and use this only as the OpenAPI schema.

_curies.description:
Ruby only emits `_curies` on the resources that actually document a
curied rel; a pacticipant is not one of them, so this is optional.

ProviderState.description: A provider state, with the consumers whose pacts use it.

ProviderStatesResponse.description: Response for the provider states endpoints (Ruby's `ProviderStatesDecorator`).

PutVersionRequest.description:
Body of `PUT /pacticipants/{name}/versions/{number}`, as Ruby's
`VersionDecorator` reads it: `number` and branches aren't writeable.

page.description:
The triggered-webhook list is not a paginated collection in Ruby — it
renders `_embedded` and `_links` only — so these carry no guarantee.

VerificationResponse.description:
Mirrors Ruby's `Api::Decorators::VerificationDecorator`.

The property names here were previously invented — `pactVersion`,
`providerVersion` and `executionDate` are served by neither broker. Ruby
renders `providerApplicationVersion` and `verificationDate`, and that is
what this documents.

_links.description:
Omitted when the pact version behind the verification has been deleted,
since every href is derived from it.

providerName.description:
Absent on the list resources, which render the provider name alongside
rather than inside each entry.

verifiedBy.description: The verifier's self-reported identity: `{}` when it reported none.

username.description:
Ruby's `WebhookRequestTemplateDecorator` carries the basic auth
credentials here, which is where `pact-broker create-webhook` sends
them. A response shows the password as `**********`.

WebhookListResponse.description:
Mirrors Ruby's `WebhooksDecorator`, which renders the collection as links
alone: each webhook is an entry in the `_links.pb:webhooks` array, with a
`pb:create` link alongside. There is no `_embedded` envelope — embedding the
full webhook documents, as this once did, is a shape the Ruby broker never
serves.

username.description:
Deprecated: accepted for compatibility with earlier versions of this
broker; `request.username` takes precedence.

updatedAt.description:
Ruby's `Timestamps` renders `updatedAt` only when it differs from
`createdAt`, so it is absent on a webhook that has never been updated.
